steps.description: A named workflow or explicit instruction is authoritative. The classifier may add required verification or approval boundaries but must not silently downgrade or replace the explicit request.
steps.name: explicit_user_workflow

steps.description: When a compatible adaptive snapshot exists, resume the existing mode and current stage; do not re-plan from the beginning; reclassify only when the repository revision, request, scope, or host capability changed materially.
steps.name: compatible_continuation

steps.description: Select long-horizon when the request explicitly requires multi-session work, durable checkpoints, repeated cycles, or a bounded continuation loop. Use the existing loop/run-state machinery.
steps.name: long_horizon_work

steps.description: Select orchestrated when one or more of these apply: security-sensitive behavior; release or publication behavior; installation or configuration ownership; destructive migration; two or more genuinely independent implementation workstreams; explicit independent review requirement; user-visible integration where failure would be materially costly.
steps.name: high_risk_or_multi_system_work

steps.description: Select planned when: acceptance criteria are incomplete; the change spans multiple systems or architectural boundaries; important implementation decisions must be resolved before editing; scope is broad but does not require a multi-agent team.
steps.name: broad_or_ambiguous_work

steps.description: Select assisted when: the repository or subsystem is unfamiliar; cross-file symbol tracing is required; the request is primarily debugging; implementation is bounded but needs exploration or specialist verification.
steps.name: unfamiliar_cross_file_or_diagnostic_work

steps.description: Select direct when the change is localized, acceptance criteria are clear, and targeted verification is sufficient.
steps.name: small_clear_low_risk_work

escalation_triggers.description: A targeted verification failure adds a debugging stage.
A failure that reveals broader scope may increase the mode by one level.
A new security, release, migration, or destructive-risk finding requires independent review.
An unavailable capability uses a fallback before increasing workflow depth.
A changed user goal produces a new decision rather than mutating the old goal invisibly.

assisted.description: Add focused repository understanding or debugging before implementation. Use one specialist responsibility when useful.

direct.description: Implement the localized change and run targeted verification. No plan artifact or subagent by default.

long-horizon.description: Use the existing loop/checkpoint mechanism around a planned or orchestrated workflow and preserve continuation state.

orchestrated.description: Divide genuinely independent responsibilities, coordinate outputs, and require independent verification or review.

planned.description: Resolve decisions and acceptance criteria before implementation. Execute the approved plan and verify it.

fields.description: Unique identifier for the adaptive decision.
fields.name: decisionId

fields.description: Digest of the original user request for compatibility checking.
fields.name: requestDigest

fields.description: Selected workflow mode (direct, assisted, planned, orchestrated, long-horizon).
fields.name: mode

fields.description: Ordered list of stages selected for this decision.
fields.name: stages

fields.description: Named responsibilities engaged for this decision.
fields.name: responsibilities

fields.description: Capability classes required for this decision.
fields.name: capabilityClasses

fields.description: Mapping of capability class to resolved provider.
fields.name: runtimeResolution

fields.description: Material reasons for the selected mode and omissions.
fields.name: reasons

fields.description: Number of automatic depth escalations applied (bounded by max_auto_escalations).
fields.name: escalationCount

fields.description: Repository revision marker for compatibility checking on resume.
fields.name: revisionMarker

fields.description: Current blocker, or null when not blocked.
fields.name: blocker

fields.description: Next action to take in the current stage.
fields.name: nextAction
